correctness.rationale: For every finite bounded lattice with at most one atom, every two nonzero elements have nonzero meet, hence semicomplementation forces neg(a)=0 for a>0; conditional identity yields neg(0)=1, so a≤neg neg(a). When two distinct atoms p,q exist, the displayed special-p row a⇒b=1 if a≤b, q if a=p and a≰b, otherwise a∧b obeys P1–P5, conditional identity and semicomplementation, but neg(p)=q and neg neg(p)=0. The P5 verification correctly distinguishes d=a∧b≤c, d=p and other d; non-distributive lattices are allowed. On B2 the only two free entries are u=p⇒0∈{0,q}, v=q⇒0∈{0,p}; exactly 4 T and 2 F and 3/2 automorphism orbits. Singleton lattice is covered; no infinite atomless claim.
